title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation scam in which AI-generated content was used to fabricate a plausible-looking interview between two real, named public figures in order to promote an unlicensed financial platform. The failure did not occur inside a regulated AI deployment, it occurred in the misuse of generative AI tools by external actors to produce convincing fake editorial content. The mechanism that would have caught it, editorial verification by a reader or platform before the content spread, was absent.

The broader pattern ASIC describes is one of scale rather than sophistication alone. AI tools allow scammers to produce large volumes of fake websites, articles, and testimonials quickly enough that takedown efforts lag behind creation. The 182 percent increase in schemes removed and the parallel rises in phishing and fake platform content suggest the bottleneck is detection speed, not the difficulty of identifying any single piece of fake content once examined.

What is not established is that any specific AI product or company is responsible for generating the fake interview, and ASIC's figures represent schemes removed rather than confirmed financial losses or convictions.

reports.title: The fake Alan Kohler interview that shows a type of scam that’s on the rise
AI deepfake scams 'an emergency in the making' as ASIC reports rise in false investment endorsements
ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception

summary:
A fake article featuring a fabricated interview between ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler and Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock has surfaced online, exemplifying a rising wave of AI-generated investment scams. The fictional piece depicted the two engaging in heated debate over Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform that Australian authorities warn against. The interview never occurred, yet such deceptive content is becoming increasingly common and sophisticated as artificial intelligence technology advances.

Australian securities regulator ASIC reports that investment scams have surged dramatically, with the watchdog removing 19,400 schemes last year, representing a 182 percent increase. The regulator identified a 279 percent jump in phishing scam takedowns and a 151 percent rise in fake investment platform removals. Scammers commonly impersonate prominent Australians including Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Alan Kohler, and billionaire Gina Rinehart, creating elaborate webs of fake websites, articles, and testimonials. ASIC urges consumers to verify Australian Financial Services license numbers and avoid investment opportunities that seem too good to be true.
